title: Cash flow and break-even set: Noor Bakes (fictional)
subject: Business
source: Written for business/y11 lesson 54 (Cash flow and break-even set with answers (teacher-written, pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 54. Noor Bakes is a fictional bakery opening a second shop. Complete the forecast, answer the break-even questions and write a recommendation.

questions.q: In which months is the closing balance negative? Suggest one halal way to cover it.
questions.a: April and May. For example: the owner puts in more capital, delays buying equipment, or asks trade customers to pay sooner (not an interest-bearing loan).

blocks.text: The second shop has fixed costs of £36,000 a year. A box of pastries sells for £20; its variable cost is £8.

questions.q: Noor Bakes expects to sell 3,600 boxes. Calculate the margin of safety and the profit.
Fixed costs rise by £6,000. Calculate the new break-even output.
Explain why a profitable business like Noor Bakes can still run out of cash.
questions.a: Profit is not cash: customers may pay late or large bills (rent, ovens) fall due before sales come in, so the balance can go negative even when sales cover costs over the year.

box.title: Should Noor Bakes open the second shop in April? Use the forecast and break-even.
